note: Triennial election of the rural district councillors, polled on Wednesday 1 June 1927, the Tyrone polling day (queue nominal 26 May). Two contests, Augher and Aughnacloy Rural; the other divisions were returned unopposed and are not printed. Filed on 1927-06-01, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Tyrone that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1927-06-02 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Nine unopposed returns are added from the Ulster Herald's nomination list (23 April 1927, p. 5). Aughnacloy Urban had two nominations (F. W. Malley (U.), Richard Vance, J.P. (Independent)) and was not polled: Mr. Malley's nomination failed because his papers were not lodged by him or his proposer or seconder, giving Richard Vance a walk-over (Northern Whig, 30 April 1927, p. 8); Foremass had no nomination, so its sitting member, Francis M'Carroll, was deemed re-elected; Augher's and Aughnacloy Rural's contests are recorded; Cullamore, Newtownsaville and Tullyvar are added from the continuation of the list (6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected (council-audit, Nov 2026): the note gave the poll as Thursday 2 June 1927; Tyrone polled on Wednesday 1 June 1927 (Mid-Ulster Mail, 4 June 1927, p. 8: "Wednesday, 1st inst."), the date the round is filed under.
